# Consumer Companist Hosting

Use only the rules that apply to the current consumer task.

## Prepare Companist hosting and external identity at foundation creation

When Companist is the requested host, generate its deployment contract and BFF identity boundary from the first increment.

## Preferred approach

When the user names Companist as the deployment target, prepare the hosting contract while creating the foundation, not after feature implementation. Companist hosting does not require adopting Companist Auth. Preserve another provider when chosen. If Companist owns identities, record `capabilities.identityOwnership: "external"`; if the app also owns customer accounts, retain local NewHeap Identity and model the external login separately. Do not convert existing apps or replace their working sign-in as a side effect of adopting this recipe.

For Companist sign-in, use a server-side BFF with OIDC authorization code and PKCE, exact HTTPS callback, state/nonce validation and `MapInboundClaims = false`. Validate issuer, signature, expiry and audience before reading claims. Bound return URLs with `NhReturnUrls`. Keep access and refresh tokens in an encrypted server-side session store with an opaque HttpOnly Secure cookie; persist Data Protection keys and sessions across deployments. Serialize refresh per session, revoke on logout and reject removed or disallowed users. Angular receives a session/claims projection and antiforgery token, never OAuth credentials. Forward NewHeap protected controller schemes to the app's session scheme with `AddNewHeapAuthenticationForwarding` when needed; this does not replace backend policies.

Fetch the authority's current access context on the server. Verify the token subject, tenant ID, OS environment ID, application ID, deployment-environment ID and dedicated client audience against the trusted runtime options and current decision. Never accept those IDs from a browser selector. Rebuild mutable application permissions per request (or a deliberately bounded cache); do not keep permissions from an old login or merge local staff roles into authority-owned permissions. Keep general control-plane permissions distinct from the application's catalog. Translate only declared application permissions to `NhPlatformClaimTypes.Permission`, and supply validated tenant membership explicitly for NewHeap division policies. When attaching to a local account, use the external provider/subject binding; email-based first linking requires the authority's explicit verified-email evidence, never an inference from the address. The sample's `SampleHostedAccessContext` demonstrates the projection boundary and denial cases, not a full OIDC implementation.

Commit `.companist/hosting.json` with schemaVersion 2, runtime `ubuntu-docker-ansible-v1`, architecture `amd64`, buildPack `dockercompose`, baseDirectory `/`, a JSON composeFile, one publicService, port, healthPath and declared required/optional secret/configuration arrays. Supply a production Dockerfile, lockfiles and .dockerignore; builds must not require runtime secrets. Compose uses private networks and named volumes, no host ports, host mounts, privileged mode or Docker socket. Give every service a healthcheck. The public readiness endpoint uses bounded checks of essential stores and pending migrations and returns no private diagnostics.

Opt into automatic sign-in registration with `companistAuth: { callbackPath: "/signin-oidc", permissions: [{ name: "example.access", description: "Open the app." }] }`, using the app's actual callback. Require `COMPANIST_AUTH_CLIENT_SECRET` as a secret and `COMPANIST_AUTH_AUTHORITY`, `COMPANIST_AUTH_CLIENT_ID`, `COMPANIST_TENANT_ID`, `COMPANIST_ENVIRONMENT_ID`, `COMPANIST_APPLICATION_ID`, `COMPANIST_DEPLOYMENT_ENVIRONMENT_ID` as configuration. Map them to the BFF's real option names in Compose, for example `CompanistAuth__Authority: "${COMPANIST_AUTH_AUTHORITY}"`. Companist supplies these values and registers the confidential client and catalog per deployment. Do not request manual client registration, guess IDs, generate the OAuth secret yourself or grant all users access. An administrator explicitly grants application access after registration.

For managed PostgreSQL, keep the database outside Compose. Declare engine `postgresql`, majorVersion 17 or 18, a required secret urlVariable, supported extensions, migrationService and a bounded migrationCommand. Use a standard PostgreSQL driver and the public schema. The migration command runs separately with the database URL only, before the web host's auth configuration is required; use versioned migrations and an advisory lock. Version 18 needs server placement. Bind publicUrlVariable to a required configuration value. Declare random app-owned keys in generatedSecrets, but never the database URL or an OAuth/provider credential. Stage with separate secrets and synthetic data. Declare workers/schedulers in backgroundServices so candidates cannot run business side effects before activation. Document non-database volume backups and restoration together with the database.

Static blockers describe genuine unresolved runtime requirements. Put optional integrations and operating recommendations in notes; never hard-code "no security review yet" as a blocker. Companist independently requires current security evidence for the exact commit and settings. These capabilities require a compatible Companist OS/Auth/runner release; they do not change standard NewHeap authentication defaults.

## Avoid

- Treating the generic bootstrap's `--docker` output as proof of a complete Companist-ready application.
- Using browser tokens, a development bypass, local administrator fallback or missing-client warnings to make an incomplete login appear functional.
- Reusing the OS client or another deployment's audience, credentials or database.
- Assuming a permission string proves tenant membership, or treating an ID token as a current authorization decision.
- Requiring optional AI, mail or third-party API credentials for startup or readiness.

## Verification

Run the foundation inspector and `node <foundation-skill>/scripts/validate-companist-hosting.mjs <consumer-root>`. The validator checks the static manifest and mappings; it is not a security approval or a runtime test. Build the API and Angular production app without runtime secrets, build the image, run migrations and readiness with a synthetic PostgreSQL database, and exercise login/callback, refresh, logout, revoked access and cross-app/deployment denial. Verify browser responses contain no credentials and that an existing sibling app still signs in after a control-plane change. Distinguish build, readiness, permitted login and production backup readiness in the handoff.

Executable evidence: `node examples/SampleProjectManagement/src/Back-end/Tests/ConsumerBootstrap/companist-hosting.test.mjs` and the `HostedAccessContextSamplesTests` filter in the sample's Core.Tests project. Existing external-identity module composition remains covered by SPM-281.
